target_customer: iPhone app developers (paying for promotion) and iOS users seeking discounted paid apps
problem: Paid iOS apps were hard to discover and users hesitated to buy; developers wanted a way to gain downloads.
business_model: Daily-deal and rebate promotion for paid iOS apps (refund via PayPal or iTunes gift card); developer revenue terms not found

founders.name: Edmond Yue
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

competitors.name: iPhoneGameRebate
competitors.what: Cash rebate on iPhone games, run by Ph03nix New Media

technical_complexity.rationale: Web and coupon-code redemption with PayPal and gift-card payouts; simple consumer web app.

defensibility.rationale: Daily-deal format for apps was easy to copy; no exclusive supply shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple controlled the App Store and later rebate-style promotions faced policy risk; no sourced incumbent action was found.

market_need_then: Paid-app discounts drew users: company claimed over 25,000 paid apps given away; Forbes and TechCrunch coverage (YC page).

brand_strength.rationale: Derivative positioning on Woot and some press, but no further brand evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Tapzilla applied the Woot daily-deal model to paid iOS apps in YC Summer 2010 and launched in October 2010. YC lists it as Acquired, but no acquirer, date or price was found; the Dealroom estimate of $500-750K enterprise value is unverified. The size and nature of the outcome cannot be assessed from public sources.
notes: Acquirer, date and price not found despite two searches. No website listed in the directory. Dealroom enterprise-value estimate ($500-750K) is aggregator-only and not recorded. TechCrunch article could not be located. iPhoneGameRebate is listed as a competitor from a PocketGamer article about AppRebates; its exact date is approximate. YC text ties AppRebates.com to Tapzilla. Web Archive skipped.
